html:
The Moneton were a Native American people of the Kanawha Valley in today's West Virginia, near where the Kanawha and New rivers meet. English explorers and traders from Virginia recorded them in the 1670s. Their name is thought to mean "big water people", and they probably spoke a Siouan language like the Tutelo and Monacan to the east.

Almost nothing else is known of them. In the late 1600s the Haudenosaunee raided widely across the Ohio valley, and the Moneton disappear from the records soon after, probably merging with other Siouan peoples of Virginia.
